claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric effect in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is governed by nanoscale ferromagnetic precipitates embedded in a soft magnetic matrix.
Nanoscale ferromagnetic precipitates reduce the energy barriers for magnetic-domain reorientation.
Reducing domain-reorientation barriers minimizes magnetic hysteresis.
A fine precipitate dispersion ensures rapid heat exchange.
A fine precipitate dispersion preserves mechanical integrity.
Controlled moderate-temperature annealing for varying durations can adjust nanoscale precipitate size and distribution.
There is an optimal precipitate scale for low-field magnetic reorientation and heat exchange.
Precipitate distributions and precipitate–matrix interfaces mediate magnetic interactions.
Precipitate distributions and precipitate–matrix interfaces mediate thermal conduction.
Nanoscale precipitates act as efficient magnetic-domain-switching sites at low applied fields.
Fine precipitate dispersion provides continuous pathways that support rapid thermal transport.
Fine precipitate dispersion prevents localized stress concentrations that could compromise mechanical stability.
Relative to the baseline state, annealed samples with optimized precipitate dispersion will exhibit a larger low-field isothermal entropy change.
Relative to the baseline state, annealed samples with optimized precipitate dispersion will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Relative to the baseline state, annealed samples with optimized precipitate dispersion will maintain or improve mechanical performance.
The unoptimized baseline has a lower magnetocaloric response and potentially greater hysteresis because of its less optimized precipitate distribution.
The proposed mechanism should apply to rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys that form similar phase structures and retain comparable precipitation behavior and matrix properties.
